conventions.representation: r = a0 + 0.a1a2..., with a0 = floor(r) and nonnegative fractional part less than 1.
conventions.overline: \overline{m}.d1d2... = -m + 0.d1d2...; the overline applies only to the integer part.
conventions.finite_tail: Append infinitely many zeros to the right of a finite decimal.
conventions.excluded_standard_form: Numerically equivalent eventually-all-nine expansions are not the selected standard form.
conventions.comparison: Compare integer parts first, then the first differing fractional digit.

tasks.derivation: 7 = 7 + 0. The standard infinite form appends zeros after the decimal point.
tasks.distinction: An integer also has a standard infinite decimal; infinitely many zero digits do not change its value.
Append zeros on the right, rather than shifting the finite digits or repeating them.
The signed integer is the floor and the decimal part is a nonnegative complement, including its leading zero.

tasks.derivation: 10 = 4*2 + 2 and 20 = 4*5 + 0, giving 0.25 followed by zero digits.
tasks.distinction: A terminating quotient keeps both nonzero quotient digits and takes a zero tail.
A negative proper fraction needs integer part -1 and the complementary positive fraction.

tasks.derivation: -2/3 = -1 + 1/3; 10 = 3*3 + 1 returns remainder 1 indefinitely, so every decimal digit is 3.
tasks.distinction: Complement the negative proper fraction before long division, and retain the nonterminating recurring tail.

tasks.derivation: Equal integer parts and first three digits; fourth fractional digits 6 < 8 settle the order.
tasks.distinction: Use the first differing digit from the left, not a later differing digit or a common truncated prefix.

tasks.derivation: Write -3 + 0.62439 and -3 + 0.62429; fourth fractional digits 3 > 2. Alternatively reverse the strict order of the positive magnitudes.
tasks.distinction: Negative-number comparison is not the unchanged order of their positive magnitudes.

tasks.derivation: Pad the finite right-hand decimal with zeros. The first three digits agree; the fourth digits are 4 > 0. The recurring tail contributes the strictly positive geometric sum 1/2250.
